data.title: Env Var
data.tagline: Provide configuration outside the source code
data.description: Environment variables supply values such as API endpoints, feature settings, and secret keys when a program starts. Public browser variables are visible to visitors, even if their names come from an environment file. Keep real secrets on the server and document the required variable names with safe examples.

use: Set different values for development and production
Turn deployment-specific features on or off
avoid: Commit a file containing real secrets
Put private keys in variables exposed to browser code
Assume changing a value updates a running process automatically

lessonPractice.title: A backend needs a third-party secret without committing it. Where should it live?

options.label: In a server-side deployment environment variable, with a real-value-free local example
options.feedback: Correct. The runtime supplies the secret; the repository keeps only its name and setup guidance.

options.label: In frontend configuration, hidden by not rendering it
options.feedback: Anything shipped to the browser can be inspected and cannot hold a secret.

options.label: In a code comment until just before release
options.feedback: It can enter history or a build artifact; temporary exposure is still exposure.

data.agentPrompt: Move this third-party secret from code into a server-side environment variable and add a real-value-free example variable name. Confirm neither git diff nor the client build contains the secret; after configuration, make one successful service call.
